$comment: Device-side policy values you expect to find under
after your Intune policy has applied.
Two blocks, and the distinction matters:
expectedDeviceRegistry  - the supported baseline. The ConfigureDeadline* family sits
under 'Manage end user experience' in the Update CSP. It is
explicitly lists Windows 11 21H2 and later. This is the layer
that actually enforces the restart, so this is the layer that
legacyWindows10Only     - the five notification-shaping policies. Microsoft documents
them as legacy and NOT applicable to Windows 11. Left disabled.
Set enabled to true only on a Windows 10 estate.
The collector always compares the supported block. It compares the legacy block only when
you enable it - and on a Windows 11 device it will tell you plainly that these values may
be present in the registry and still do nothing.
Adjust the values to match your own ring, then run Get-UpdateEvidence.ps1.

$notes.ConfigureDeadlineForFeatureUpdates: days until a feature update installs regardless of active hours. Range 0-30
$notes.ConfigureDeadlineGracePeriod: days between installation and the automatic restart. VERIFIED on a managed Windows 11 device: an Intune update ring writes this GENERIC value name, not ConfigureDeadlineGracePeriodForFeatureUpdates. The feature-update-specific variant appears only if you set it explicitly via the Settings Catalog; when absent, Windows falls back to this one.
$notes.ConfigureDeadlineNoAutoReboot: 1 = do not auto-restart before the deadline. This is what turns the grace period into a real window rather than a suggestion.
$notes.$providerSuffixes: The device also carries <Name>_ProviderSet and <Name>_WinningProvider beside each value. WinningProvider is the GUID of the channel that won the setting - the signal to look at when two policies fight over the same CSP.
$notes.$verified: Value names confirmed on an Intune-enrolled Windows 11 24H2 device on 2026-09-04 by reading HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\PolicyManager\current\device\Update directly.

$warning: WINDOWS 10 ONLY. All five settings below are legacy policies that Microsoft documents
as not applicable to Windows 11 and liable to removal. Raised by James Robinson,
Intune & Windows MVP. See the correction at the top of the README.
They may still be delivered into the registry on Windows 11 and do nothing:
delivered and honoured are different claims.

$notes.SetAutoRestartNotificationDisable: 0 = notifications ENABLED. The label is inverted: 1 disables them
